records.name: Preservation Alliance for Greater Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that works to protect Philadelphia's old buildings and neighborhoods. Its volunteer guides lead weekend walking tours from May through November, each one covering a different part of the city.
records.what_you_do: Guides lead tours that last 1.5 to 2 hours, rain or shine. Experienced volunteers from many backgrounds serve as guides, and the site links a Become a Guide page.

schedule.text: Volunteer-led tours on weekends from May through November. Saturday tours usually start at 10 am and Sunday tours at 2 pm. Fall listings run October 3 to November 15, 2026.

locations.label: Neighborhood walking tours (meeting points vary by tour)

cost.text: Tickets are bought online in advance, and public ticket prices are not shown on the page we checked. Private tours need a $200 deposit for up to 10 people, and students and ACCESS card holders can ask for discounts on regular tours.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for a listed tour, or email info@preservationalliance.com to ask about becoming a guide
first_step.basis: Public tours are open to anyone who buys a ticket. The guide path is mentioned but not explained in detail.

records.notes: Office at One Penn Center, 1617 John F. Kennedy Blvd, Suite 850, Philadelphia. The tour listings on the page do not state a year, but the dates match 2026 weekdays. The site also lists a Fall Speaker Series and an Architectural Dinner.

records.name: Association of Philadelphia Tour Guides
records.summary: A membership group for people who guide visitors around Philadelphia, both paid and volunteer guides. It runs a certification program for city guides and keeps members connected through training and events.
records.what_you_do: Members take part in the city guide education and certification program, get training, and share industry events and news.

schedule.text: The office is open weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm. A 2027 membership drive is mentioned, with no dates given.

first_step.how: Join through the Join APT membership page, or contact the office
first_step.basis: Joining is by membership, and the page does not show dues or a meeting schedule, so the way in is not clear to a newcomer.

records.notes: A search result described monthly meetings on the second Wednesday, but the page we read lists no meeting dates, so those are not recorded. The site copyright runs 2018 to 2025. The 2026 job fair vendor list and the 2027 membership drive are mentioned without months. Membership figures on the page are 270 or more members in 2026.

records.name: Friends of Mount Moriah Cemetery
records.summary: Volunteers who clean up and restore Mount Moriah Cemetery in southwest Philadelphia. They hold clean-up days one or two times a month, and you can come to just one.
records.what_you_do: Clear brush, trim weeds, pick up trash, plant flowers, and help with historical research on the grounds. Groups from colleges and businesses also come to clean-up days.

schedule.text: Clean-up events one or two times a month, through the year. A Saturday event was planned for April 25, 2026. Dates are posted on the group's volunteer page.

locations.label: Mount Moriah Cemetery, Philadelphia entrance on Kingsessing Avenue

cost.text: Free to volunteer. Donations help pay for flowers planted on the grounds.

first_step.how: Pick a clean-up day from the volunteer page, or email info@fommci.org
first_step.basis: Clean-up days are open to community members, students and groups, and a volunteer can attend one event without any long-term commitment.

records.notes: The volunteer day page we checked is from September 2021, so it is not used as current evidence. An older Hidden City article said the cemetery's ownership is unresolved and that volunteers may clear grounds but not work on buildings or monuments. That may be out of date, so ask before planning structure work.

records.name: Friends of Laurel Hill and West Laurel Hill Cemeteries
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps look after two historic cemeteries, Laurel Hill in Philadelphia and West Laurel Hill in Bala Cynwyd. Volunteers help restore monuments and grounds, and the group runs tours and events.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers help with grounds upkeep, restoration, and the group's education and outreach programs. The cemetery is free to visit every day.

schedule.text: Gates are open 7 am to 7 pm from spring through fall, and 7 am to 5 pm in winter. The support page we read lists no specific volunteer dates.

cost.text: Admission is free every day. The group is supported by donations, memberships and sponsorships.

first_step.how: Sign up on the volunteer page at laurelhillphl.com/support/volunteer
first_step.basis: Volunteers of all ages and backgrounds are welcome through a public sign-up page, but the page describes no beginner program.

records.notes: No dated events were on the support page. The Halloween festivities are mentioned without dates. The support page says the group's programs include tours and education, but no 2026 dated items were found.

records.name: Germantown Historical Society
records.summary: An education and research center that keeps the history of Germantown and the old German Township. Volunteers help researchers, catalog photos, and care for the library and collections.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers transcribe oral histories, scan and catalog photos, rehouse collections, and help researchers at the Pat Henning Library and Archives.

schedule.text: Volunteers give a few free hours each week, on a schedule they set with the library. Research visits are by appointment.

cost.text: No prices are listed on the pages we checked.

first_step.how: Email library@germantownhistory.org or call 215-844-1683, ext. 104, to say how many free hours you have each week
first_step.basis: The site invites new volunteers to get in touch by email, and no experience requirement is stated.

records.notes: The society's own site shows copyright 2008 to 2024 and a public notice that appears to date from early 2025, so its own news is thin. Its October 2026 film screenings at the society are listed on the Historic Germantown site. The Oktoberfest and Awbury volunteering seen in an older search result is not recorded.

records.name: Historic Germantown
records.summary: A partnership of about 20 historic houses, museums and gardens in northwest Philadelphia. Its sites offer tours, free events and a volunteer garden program at Wyck.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers at Wyck's Home Farm Club help in the kitchen garden on Tuesdays and Fridays, get short lessons, and take home a share of fresh produce. No sign-up is required.

schedule.text: Wyck garden helpers come on Tuesdays and Fridays. Events run through fall 2026, including Saturday and Sunday tours and workshops in October and November.

locations.label: Partner sites across Germantown, Mount Airy and Chestnut Hill

cost.text: Many events are free. A Cliveden walking tour is $20, or $10 for members and for residents of 19119 and 19144.

first_step.how: For the Wyck garden, come on a Tuesday or Friday with no sign-up needed. For other questions, email programs@historicgermantownpa.org
first_step.basis: The garden program offers short lessons and needs no registration, so beginners can start on their first visit.

records.notes: The Wyck garden times are given as days only. The rotating exhibit end date is listed as December 1, 2026 in one place and December 1, 2027 in another, so no end date is recorded. Mailing address: 6711 Germantown Ave, Suite 4936, Philadelphia, PA 19119. The site also lists a 2026 membership drive.

records.name: Philadelphia Society for the Preservation of Landmarks
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs four 18th century historic houses: Powel House, Hill-Physick House, Grumblethorpe and Historic Waynesborough. It has a youth volunteer program at Grumblethorpe.
records.what_you_do: Youth volunteers can join the Grumblethorpe program. The site does not describe adult volunteer roles.

schedule.text: Visit and event times are on the site's visit page. The text we read gives no event dates.

locations.label: Main office, near the Powel House

first_step.how: Call 215-925-2251 or use the contact page to ask about the Grumblethorpe Youth Volunteers program
first_step.basis: The site names the youth program but does not say how to apply or what the roles are, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The site copyright shows 2023, which is not counted as evidence. No dated news was on the page. The site also lists Road Scholar, education and cultural programs, and private event rentals. Adult volunteer roles need a separate check.

records.name: Fort Mifflin on the Delaware
records.summary: A historic fort on the Delaware River in southwest Philadelphia, run by a nonprofit. It offers guided tours, school trips, scout activities and paranormal programs, and it rents its grounds for events.
records.what_you_do: The site we read does not describe volunteer roles. Support is through donations and a Join The Fort membership.

schedule.text: A candlelight ghost tour is listed for October 9 at 7 pm. The page does not state the year.

locations.label: Fort Mifflin, at Fort Mifflin Road and Hog Island Road

cost.text: Admission is not listed. Candlelight tours need timed tickets bought in advance.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us page at fortmifflin.us/contact-us/ to ask about volunteering
first_step.basis: The site does not list volunteer roles or how to sign up.

records.notes: The October 9 ghost tour page does not state a year, and its event link suggests 2024, so the date is not treated as current. A search result mentioned a volunteer phone line and a 2026 living history day. Neither is confirmed on the site, so neither is recorded. Recheck before publishing.

records.name: Friends of Jewish Cemeteries
records.summary: Volunteers who clean up and restore historic Jewish cemeteries in the Philadelphia area, including Har Nebo in Northeast Philadelphia. The work is hands-on, and some volunteers help with burial records.
records.what_you_do: Cut vines, weed trees, pick up trash, support headstone restoration pilots with professional conservators, and help digitize burial records at Har Jehuda.

schedule.text: Cleanup dates are not listed on the page we checked. Join the mailing list to hear about them.

locations.label: Har Nebo Cemetery, Oxford Circle, Northeast Philadelphia

cost.text: No volunteer fee is mentioned. Optional donations go to a cemetery restoration fund.

first_step.how: Join the mailing list, or email jlasday@jewishphilly.org to ask about getting involved
first_step.basis: No sign-up process is published, so a newcomer has to ask to join the list or contact staff first.

records.notes: The page has no dated events and links to older news coverage. It names Har Jehuda, where records are digitized with the Jewish Genealogical and Archival Society of Greater Philadelphia. A search result named the Jewish Federation of Greater Philadelphia as the parent organization, which the page itself does not confirm.

records.name: Penn Museum
records.summary: A museum in University City. Its Cartifacts volunteers set up carts of five to ten artifacts in the galleries and talk with visitors about each object's history and use.
records.what_you_do: Set up themed carts of artifacts in the galleries, then explain each object to visitors of all ages. Each cart is tied to a gallery, and volunteers pick the subject they want to learn.

schedule.text: Shifts run Tuesday to Sunday, 10 am to 4 pm. Volunteers commit to at least 4 hours a month, and weekend volunteers are especially needed.

first_step.how: Submit the online application for the Cartifacts opportunity, or email volunteer@pennmuseum.org
first_step.basis: Volunteers must apply for a listed role, reviews are on a rolling basis, and no beginner training is described.

records.notes: The older gallery docent program, mentioned in a 2016 posting, could not be confirmed as open in 2026. The listing does not state a deadline or start date.

records.name: Independence Seaport Museum
records.summary: A museum at 211 S. Columbus Blvd with historic ships and boats. Its docent program trains volunteers to lead tours of the museum and its ships, but it is not taking new applications right now.
records.what_you_do: Docents lead tours of the museum and its historic ships, help with education programs, and welcome guests at special events. Training runs four sessions in late February and early March.

schedule.text: Docent training is four sessions in late February and early March. Docent tours run year round on weekdays and weekends.

first_step.how: No applications right now. Check the volunteer page later, or call 215-413-8655
first_step.basis: The museum says it has reached its volunteer capacity, so new docents are not being taken at this time.

records.notes: Published so visitors can see the program and check back. The page gives no reopening date. Other volunteer roles at the South Street Seaport Museum, a separate organization, were seen in a search result and are not recorded here.

records.name: Philadelphia Archaeological Forum
records.summary: A group that shares Philadelphia's archaeology with the public and speaks up to protect historic sites. It hosts public talks, runs a historical burial grounds map and database, and invites people to join advocacy actions.
records.what_you_do: Attend public talks, sign petitions, and send public comments to the City Planning Commission during its reviews. The group has no formal volunteer roles listed.

schedule.text: Public talks on specific dates in fall 2026, including an October 12 Indigenous Peoples Day event and an October 21 Penn Museum talk. Pennsylvania Archaeology Month runs in October.

cost.text: Some talks are free. A Penn Museum talk on October 21 costs $10 general admission, $5 virtual, and is free for members.

first_step.how: Attend a public talk, many of which need registration. To ask about involvement, use the contact form at phillyarchaeology.net/about/contact-paf/
first_step.basis: Public talks are open to anyone, though some need registration, and no formal volunteer route is described.

records.notes: Dated items on the page: July 15, 2026 (news about panels at the President's House site), August 27, 2026 (open letter), and October talks. The page does not give the year for some February items, so those are not used.

leads_only.name: Friends of Campbell Square
leads_only.note: Port Richmond park group named in search results. Only a Facebook page was found, no group website, and no 2026 news. Not checked further.

leads_only.name: Fairmount Park Conservancy
leads_only.note: Checked for history programs. Its park stewardship and We Walk PHL programs belong to the nature lane, so a nature lane agent should take it up. Its 2026 Love Your Park and Cobbs Creek events are listed on its site.

leads_only.name: Historic Fair Hill cleanup volunteers
leads_only.note: Named in a January 2026 article as a Germantown cleanup site. No group website was seen. Check whether the site has its own volunteer page.

leads_only.name: Bella Vista Neighbors Association, historic preservation committee
leads_only.note: Search result says volunteers identify and nominate buildings for the city register. Not fetched.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Trans Oral History Project
leads_only.note: A Penn and William Way Center oral history project. Unknown whether it recruits community volunteers. Not fetched.

blocked.note: Historical Society of Pennsylvania volunteer page returned HTTP 403, reached through a 301 from portal.hsp.org. The HSP is a major volunteer lead and should be retried by a later agent or checked by hand.

notes: Searches: 9 of 10 used (one left unused). Fetches: about 24. Checked and dropped without a record: Woodlands Cemetery (the fetched site lists no volunteer, tour or event information, and the Grave Gardeners program was seen only on a blog and could not be confirmed); Historic Strawberry Mansion (site has a Get Involved section with no details, no contact route to volunteering). Out of area or out of family, not recorded: Heritage Conservancy (Bucks County), Preservation Pennsylvania (statewide), Eden Cemetery (Collingdale, Delaware County), Athenaeum Young Friends and Friends of Tanner House (named in search results, not fetched, no URL confirmed). Genealogical Society of Pennsylvania was suggested in a search result as the place to ask about volunteering; its site was not fetched. Most records are probably_active or active on dated 2026 evidence, but several have only undated working sites, so status is conservative. Friends of Campbell Square is a lead only because no group website exists.
